Needs changes before merge.

Safety-tier review. This PR changes posted G-code.

The new tests check all six posts. The helper checks all segments before it writes a block. No goldens moved. No UI files changed.

Requested before merge:

1. **P1: Keep rotary motion correct when an arc is split.** `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:945` and `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps:1127` put every rotary target on the first segment. The new half-circle split thus changes the tool orientation along the path. I reproduced this with both posts. The input starts at X10 Y0 Z0 A0. It commands a CCW half-circle to X-10 Y0 Z0 A90, with center X0 Y0. The machine has an A rotary about +X and enables RTCP. Fanuc writes these blocks without warnings:

   ```gcode
   G03 X0. Y10. Z0. R10. A90. F600
   G03 X-10. Y0. Z0. R10. F600
   ```

   A reaches 90 degrees at the midpoint and stays there. The intended midpoint is A45. Upstream main writes one half-circle with A90 at its endpoint. This change can cut with the wrong tool orientation. Interpolate each changing rotary angle across the segments and check its rate for each segment. Alternatively, use the original I/J/K arc when a rotary changes. Add tests for Fanuc and Doosan that check the intermediate angles and rotary rates.

Local results, with upstream/main `e3ca44fa705d71438a8fd8a8efccbafcc2b6517f`:

- Trial merge: clean. The PR already contains this main commit.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 42 post suites passed, with 319 tests. The 75 app suites had 531 passed, one failed, and one ignored test.
- The app failure is `first_4axis_part::the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`. I repeated it with all six post files restored to upstream main. It fails with the same diagnostic before posting:

  ```text
  the machine check: "Flat A-90: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting"
  ```

  This failure exists on main. It is not an additional requested change for this PR.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-post --test radius_arcs`: five passed after restoration.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Mutation 1: removed the Fanuc radius-mismatch guard. The test failed on `fanuc/mismatch`, which wrote `R-5.5`. Restored: green.
- Mutation 2: removed the Fanuc positive-radius and rounded-chord checks. The test failed on `fanuc/tiny_inch`, which wrote `R0.`. Restored: green.
- The rotary reproduction above fails the expected midpoint-angle check on this head. It is separate from the two successful guard mutations.

All commands ran locally. No GitHub runner ran. No code changes remain. Batch and release gates were not run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: P1 rotary motion on split arcs in Fanuc and Doosan.

Both posts now keep the original I/J/K arc when the block writes rotary words. This preserves continuous orientation and the existing feed cap.

Tests in `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs`:
- `fanuc_rotary_half_turn_keeps_continuous_angles_and_rate`
- `doosan_rotary_half_turn_keeps_continuous_angles_and_rate`

Both tests check forward and reverse turns, midpoint A45, endpoint angles, feed caps, and rotary rates. They also check fixed-angle radius splitting.
Removing each post's fix made its test fail. Restoring both fixes made all seven radius tests pass.

Quick gate against `upstream/main`: red only for the known main failure in `first_4axis_part::the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`. It reports "Flat A-90: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting". The post suites passed 321 tests. The app suites passed 531 tests, failed one, and ignored one.

Clippy passed for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`, with all targets and warnings denied.

New head: d98f06f1e99595a42f80c6ca3f12e77c1f0e90fe.
Please review this head again.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings remain.

Safety-tier review: this PR changes posted G-code. I checked the laws against the current upstream main AGENTS.md.

The previous P1 finding is resolved. Fanuc and Doosan keep one native I/J/K arc when the block writes rotary words. The existing feed cap stays in effect. The new tests check both turn directions, endpoint angles, the implied midpoint angle, feed caps, and rotary rates. Fixed-angle arcs still use radius segments.

The six helpers check all planned segments before they write a block. The tests read the posted G-code and check reachability and reconstructed centers. No goldens moved. No UI files changed, so before/after screenshots are not required.

Local results against upstream/main `e3ca44fa705d71438a8fd8a8efccbafcc2b6517f`:

- Trial merge: clean. The PR already contains this main commit. GitHub reports MERGEABLE.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all 42 post suites passed, with 321 tests. The 75 app suites had 531 passed, one failed, and one ignored test.
- The app failure is `first_4axis_part::the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`. I repeated that test with all six post scripts restored to upstream main. It failed with the same diagnostic before posting:

  ```text
  the machine check: "Flat A-90: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting"
  ```

  This failure exists on main. It is not a new failure from this PR.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-post --test radius_arcs`: all seven tests passed after the mutations were restored.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

I ran these mutations locally:

1. Removed the Fanuc radius-mismatch guard. The test failed on `fanuc/mismatch`, which wrote `R-5.5`.
2. Removed the Fanuc positive-radius and rounded-chord checks. The test failed on `fanuc/tiny_inch`, which wrote `R0.`.
3. Removed the Fanuc rotary fallback guard. Its rotary regression test failed. The output put A90 on the first quadrant.
4. Removed the Doosan rotary fallback guard. Its rotary regression test failed with the same early rotary target.

All four mutations were red. After restoration, all seven radius tests were green. The worktree has no code changes.

Requested before merge: none. This review clears the previous rotary finding on the older head.

All commands ran locally in the foreground. No GitHub runner ran. Batch and release gates were not run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
